description: This course provides state-of-the-art speed control techniques used in modern drives for high-performance requirements.

syllabus.title: Converter Fed DC Drives
syllabus.body: Basics of electric drives, types of drives, torque-speed characteristics, multi-quadrant operation, methods of DC motor control. DC-DC converter fed DC motor drives and their control techniques, non-regenerative controlled rectifiers, fully controlled converters, single-phase half controlled and fully controlled AC-DC converter fed DC motor drives, three-phase fully controlled AC-DC converter fed DC motor drives, field control, switching systems for DC motors, chopper regulators, analysis, performance and stability of variable speed DC drives.

syllabus.title: High-Performance Control of Induction Machines for EV Drives
syllabus.body: Voltage source inverter fed induction motor drive in open loop, frequency and voltage control in PWM VSI, current source inverter fed induction motor drives. Introduction to field-oriented control (vector control), direct torque control and parameter sensitivity.

syllabus.title: High-Performance Control of Synchronous Machines
syllabus.body: Introduction, three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine modelling, torque control of a PMSM and parameter sensitivity.

syllabus.title: Application of Intelligent Controllers for AC and DC Drives
syllabus.body: Introduction to ANN, fuzzy logic and ANFIS. Implementation of ANN, fuzzy and ANFIS on DC and AC drives.

outcomes: Describe various industrial DC motors and drive systems.
Apply knowledge of power electronics to AC drive systems.
Learn advanced control methods of EV based motor drive systems.
Understand intelligent control methods of EV based AC motor drives.
